title: Migration chain and rollback class v1
description: The ordered chain of storage migrations and, for each, whether a binary rollback is available. docs/operations/DATA_LIFECYCLE_AND_RECOVERY.md is the normative owner and packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql#storage_migrations is the persistence owner. D-074 permits automatic binary rollback only while the previous release stays read/write compatible with every committed local-state and database mutation; this record is where that condition stops being something an operator remembers. The rollback class and the presence of a down section are separate fields on purpose: dropping a column back is syntactically valid and loses everything written into it, so a present down section is not reversibility and conflating the two is how a forward-only migration acquires a rollback plan nobody tested.

steps.description: Ordered. A chain with a gap is not a chain: D-097 numbers goose migrations sequentially and applies them as a deliberate operator step, so a missing version is an unapplied migration rather than a numbering style.

version.description: The goose migration version, matching a row in schema_migrations.

rollback_class.description: binary-reversible: the previous binary reads and writes the post-migration shape, so a rollback is a binary swap and nothing else. forward-only: it does not, so recovery is roll-forward or restoration of a verified pre-migration snapshot. snapshot-required: forward-only, and a verified snapshot must exist before the migration runs.

down_sql_present.description: Whether the migration file carries an explicit down section, which D-097 requires of every goose migration. It is a fact about the file and not a claim about reversibility.

pre_migration_snapshot_digest.description: Required exactly when rollback_class is snapshot-required. A snapshot-required step with no recorded snapshot is a migration that has removed its own recovery path.

minimum_binary_version.description: The oldest binary that may run against the post-migration shape. ADR-018 makes readiness return success only when the applied migration version is inside the binary's declared range, so this is the number that check reads.

irreversible_operations.description: What made the step forward-only, named rather than implied. A step that is forward-only for no recorded reason is one nobody can later re-examine.
